Walmart announces it will officially roll out Apple Pay support starting next week. The retailer has refused to offer Apple Pay support for over a decade, despite years of consumer pressure.

Apple Pay 終於登陸沃爾瑪

Walmart announced the news in a press release today. Starting August 24, the company will begin rolling out contactless payment options, including Apple Pay, at select Walmart and Sam's Club locations. Full coverage across all U.S. stores is expected by the end of this year, with gas stations adding support by mid-2027.

Walmart is broadly expanding its contactless payment support, including Apple Pay on iPhone and Apple Watch, Google Pay, contactless credit and debit cards, and other payment platforms. Customers can also add their Walmart and Sam's Club membership cards to platforms like Apple Wallet. Contactless payment will coexist with existing payment methods, including Walmart's own payment service, Walmart Pay.

公司表示：

Walmart was one of the last major retailers to hold out on Apple Pay, making this a significant win for consumers. For years, the retailer resisted adopting contactless payment, instead pushing its own QR code-based payment system, Walmart Pay.

Until last year, Walmart still firmly believed that Walmart Pay was more convenient for consumers than Apple Pay. However, to use Walmart Pay, users had to first add a debit or credit card within the Walmart app on their iPhone, then scan a QR code at checkout to complete the payment with their iPhone.

A quick search on social media reveals just how frustrated users have been with Walmart's refusal to support Apple Pay.

After all, other long-time holdouts against Apple Pay — including Kroger, Home Depot, and H-E-B — changed course years ago, and not without reason.

Walmart's lack of Apple Pay support — has it affected your shopping habits? With Apple Pay coming to Walmart and Sam's Club, will it make you more inclined to shop there? Let us know in the comments.
